description: Two thresholds and two signals, giving comparisons between the signals, each signal clipped and folded between the thresholds, and gates saying where each signal is relative to them

params.text: Sets the upper threshold, -10V to +10V, or in the additive position of the three-way switch the distance above the lower threshold
Chooses how the two thresholds combine: centred collapses both to their midpoint when they cross, inversing swaps them, and additive reads the upper knob as a distance above the lower
Rounds both signals to 0V or 10V before the comparisons and the two waveshapers, so they are judged as bits; the six gates that test against the thresholds keep reading the unrounded signals
Rescales the clipped and folded outputs so that the span between the two thresholds comes out as ±5V however narrow that span is

inputs.text: Multiplies the lower threshold knob by a tenth of this voltage, so 10V gives the knob's own setting and a patched cable at 0V puts the threshold at 0V
Multiplies the upper threshold knob by a tenth of this voltage, so 10V gives the knob's own setting and a patched cable at 0V puts it at 0V
One of the two signals compared and shaped here; with its own jack empty the module puts a fresh random voltage there every sample, within ±5V of the other signal or ±10V if that one is empty too
Freezes both signals at the values they held on the last rising edge here, so the outputs step rather than glide; with nothing patched both signals run free

outputs.text: The lower threshold as the module is using it; in the centred position of the three-way switch it becomes the midpoint of the two knobs whenever the lower would be above the upper
The upper threshold as the module is using it; in the additive position of the three-way switch it is the lower threshold plus the upper knob
10V while the A signal is above the B signal, 0V otherwise
10V while the A signal is below the B signal, 0V otherwise
10V while the two signals are exactly equal, 0V otherwise, which two free-running voltages almost never are unless binary mode is on
10V while the two signals differ, 0V otherwise
The A signal with everything outside the two thresholds flattened onto the nearer one
The B signal with everything outside the two thresholds flattened onto the nearer one
The A signal folded back between the two thresholds, reflected at each one until it is inside, up to fifty reflections
The B signal folded back between the two thresholds, reflected at each one until it is inside, up to fifty reflections
10V while the A signal is below the lower threshold, 0V otherwise
10V while the B signal is below the lower threshold, 0V otherwise
10V while the A signal is above the upper threshold, 0V otherwise
10V while the B signal is above the upper threshold, 0V otherwise
10V while the A signal is between the two thresholds, the thresholds themselves counted as inside
10V while the B signal is between the two thresholds, the thresholds themselves counted as inside

notes: both threshold knobs come up at 0V, which leaves no span between them, so the clipped and folded outputs read 0V until a knob is moved
leave the A or B jack empty and the module fills it with a fresh random voltage on every sample, which makes it a noise source; a trigger at the s&h input turns that into stepped random values

inputs.2:
±10V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads a fresh random voltage each sample.
inputs.3:
±10V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads a fresh random voltage each sample.
inputs.4:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
